import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Specifications Analysis (1000 Cameras)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(df['sensor_type'].unique()))

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
for i, sensor in enumerate(df['sensor_type'].unique()):
    mask = df['sensor_type'] == sensor
    ax1.scatter(df.loc[mask, 'megapixels'], df.loc[mask, 'price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, s=30)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left', fontsize=8)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_prices = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=len(brand_prices))
bars = ax2.barh(brand_prices.index, brand_prices.values, color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Brand (Top 10 Brands)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
# Add value labels
for bar, val in zip(bars, brand_prices.values):
    ax2.text(val + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${val:.0f}', 
             va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Distribution of Cameras by Body Type and 4K Video Capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=['#ff7f0e', '#1f77b4'], edgecolor='black', width=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Count by Body Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video', fontsize=10)
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Model Year Trend - Average Megapixels and Max ISO over time
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year').agg({
    'megapixels': 'mean',
    'max_iso': 'mean'
}).reset_index()

color1 = '#2ecc71'
color2 = '#e74c3c'

ax4_twin = ax4.twinx()
line1 = ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['megapixels'], 
                  color=color1, marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=5, label='Avg Megapixels')
line2 = ax4_twin.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['max_iso'], 
                       color=color2, marker='s', linewidth=2, markersize=5, label='Avg Max ISO')

ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Average Megapixels', fontsize=11, color=color1)
ax4_twin.set_ylabel('Average Max ISO', fontsize=11, color=color2)
ax4.set_title('Camera Specifications Evolution Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color1)
ax4_twin.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color2)
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Combine legends
lines1, labels1 = ax4.get_legend_handles_labels()
lines2, labels2 = ax4_twin.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax4.legend(lines1 + lines2, labels1 + labels2, loc='upper left', fontsize=9)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
